topic_name: QA calibration on disputed tie decisions
summary: Two QA tutors report ties marked wrong; a tutor also reports that a similar pair received a different QA judgment from the previous day. The team lead acknowledged inconsistent QA feedback and asked for both rationales to calibrate before changing the tie threshold. The current FAQ calls for the pairs, relevant prompt constraints and both rationales, with a check that the cases are actually comparable.

severity.rationale: Two distinct QA tutors and a tutor report comparable disputed tie judgments within the supplied batch context, suggesting a broader QA-consistency risk rather than only one unanswered pair. The evidence does not establish the full extent of affected work or that any disputed label is independently incorrect.

matched_signals.signal_text: Multiple distinct people or affected tasks reporting a comparable problem within the relevant project, batch, and time window, suggesting broader disruption or systemic labeling risk. Consider the number affected relative to the known active group when that information is available; do not require an explicit statement of widespread impact
matched_signals.support: Two QA tutors report ties marked wrong, and a tutor reports different QA judgments on similar pairs; these are three distinct reporting authors, not three separate people inferred from the topic's member entries.

affected_reporters.basis: Distinct authors whose own cited message reports the problem; other participants are not counted.

recommended_action.draft_text: Please prepare the disputed batch-15 pairs for a QA calibration review, including RP-9595. For each comparison, provide the pair, relevant prompt constraints and both written QA rationales. We will check whether the cases are actually comparable and apply the current criterion: choose a tie when neither response has a meaningful quality advantage; cosmetic phrasing alone does not justify a preference. Explain the user-facing benefit for any preference based on a small difference. For the RP-9595 discussion, this follows the team lead's request to calibrate before changing the tie threshold. Arrange the review once the case inputs are available.
recommended_action.scope_note: This proposes a review of the reported batch-15 disputes, not a new threshold, a batch-wide relabeling decision or automatic acceptance of every disputed tie; the team lead's existing instruction applies to the RP-9595 thread.
recommended_action.label: Schedule a short review session
recommended_action.instruction: Arrange a QA calibration review of the disputed batch-15 pairs after collecting the pairs, relevant prompt constraints and both rationales, using the current tie criterion before considering any threshold change.
recommended_action.rationale: Comparing the actual cases and rationales addresses the reported QA inconsistency without treating pair-specific replies as a blanket ruling. The earlier batch's review improved agreement in its sample, but it does not establish the outcome for this batch.

reasoning: What the evidence shows: A QA tutor reports that QA marked their tie wrong again. A QA tutor reports that a tie score passed the previous week but was flagged on near-identical tasks that day, and later reports another tie marked wrong on task RP-9595. A tutor reports that a QA reviewer accepted a tie the previous day, while a similar pair was marked wrong that day. A QA tutor replies that the pair in the first thread justifies a tie because neither response has a meaningful quality advantage, and suggests a calibration check rather than a policy rewrite for the two disputed tasks. A QA tutor replies that the pair in the second thread justifies a tie because neither response has a meaningful quality advantage, and asks that the same criterion be used for comparable pairs. A QA tutor asks whether the written QA rationales can be compared against the same rubric criterion. In the thread about RP-9595, the team lead acknowledges inconsistent QA feedback and asks for both rationales so calibration can happen before changing the tie threshold. The current project-wide FAQ says to share disputed pairs, relevant prompt constraints and both rationales for calibration, check whether the cases are actually comparable, and avoid generalizing a pair-specific answer without matching its scope. The current project-wide instructions say to choose a tie when neither response has a meaningful quality advantage; cosmetic phrasing alone does not justify a preference, and a small difference requires an explanation of its user-facing benefit. The earlier approval record authorized an announcement and an eight-pair calibration exercise for batch 14 using the existing criterion, not a new numerical threshold; that approval did not record completion. The batch-14 follow-up records reviewer agreement increasing from two to seven of eight sampled pairs after calibration, with one pair still disputed; it limits the result to that sample and says a new batch needs its own evidence. The September 16 batch-14 announcement asks for both rationales for disputed pairs at an eight-pair calibration review and describes the exercise as clarification of the existing criterion, not a new numerical threshold.
